extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.anchor: # Defaults baked into the model. Anyone who runs "ollama run shellcoach"
extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.title: Baked-in default parameters
note: **Runtime defaults that ship inside the model, so no caller has to remember them.**
- Same `num_predict` you set by hand in Lab 1 - now permanent

extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.anchor: # The persona and the rules. This is prepended to every conversation.
extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.title: The persona and its rules
note: **Four output rules the model follows on every request, without the user asking.**
- Command first in a code block, then at most three bullets
- Rule 3 (`CAUTION:` on destructive commands) is what you test in step 12

extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.anchor: # A seeded example exchange so the model copies the format above.
extra/Modelfile-shellcoach-complete.txt.title: Few-shot format priming
note: **A fake prior exchange the model imitates - the cheapest way to lock in a format.**
- Shows the answer style instead of describing it
- Multi-line values need `"""` quotes; a bare ``` fence fails `ollama create`

extra/chat_app-complete.txt.title: The streaming chat call
note: **Sends the whole conversation to Ollama and prints the reply as it streams back.**
- Same `model` / `messages` / `options` you sent by hand with curl in step 4
- `reply` accumulates the pieces so the answer can go into history

extra/chat_app-complete.txt.anchor: # Append the model's own answer so the next turn has the full context.
extra/chat_app-complete.txt.title: The app's entire memory
note: **This one line is the whole "memory" of the app - Ollama itself stores nothing.**
- Step 10 comments it out to prove exactly that
- Removing it drops only what the *model* said; your own turns stay
